summary: The main article describes the development of a novel diazabenzacenaphthenium photocatalyst (NBAP) for the four-electron reduction of esters. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope schemes for alcohol synthesis and cross-pinacol coupling, and detailed mechanistic studies including electrochemical and computational analysis.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Multielectron Reduction of Esters
items.description: Illustrates the general concept of photocatalytic four-electron reduction of esters to carbinol anions, followed by protonation to alcohols or 1,2-addition to carbonyls.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Photocatalytic Reduction of Methyl Picolinate (1a)
items.description: Shows the specific model reaction of methyl picolinate being reduced to pyridin-2-ylmethanol using NBAP and ammonium oxalate.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Reduction of Methyl Picolinate (1a) a
items.description: Optimization table screening various photocatalysts, electron sources, and control conditions for the reduction of methyl picolinate.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Multielectron Reduction of Esters a
items.description: Displays the substrate scope for the reduction of various aromatic and heteroaromatic esters to their corresponding alcohols.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: 1,2-Addition of Esters to Aldehydes or Ketones a
items.description: Shows the scope of the reductive cross-pinacol coupling between esters and aldehydes or ketones to form unsymmetric 1,2-diols.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Preparation of NBAP
items.description: Describes the one-step rhodium-catalyzed synthesis of the NBAP photocatalyst from 2-phenyl-4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazole and hex-3-yne.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: (A) Absorption and emission spectra. (B) Cyclic voltammetry of NBAP . (C) Electrochemical properties of NBAP .
items.description: Presents the photophysical and electrochemical characterization data for the NBAP catalyst, including redox potentials.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Calculated redox properties of NBAP -related structures
items.description: Compares the calculated oxidation and reduction potentials of NBAP with other related nitrogen-doped polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.

items.heading: Figure 3
items.caption: Mechanistic studies. (A) Deuteration experiment. (B) Fluorescence-quenching experiments. (C) Proposed mechanism.
items.description: Combines experimental evidence from deuteration and quenching studies to propose a catalytic cycle involving sequential SET steps.
